Here’s how to cover yourself with alerts using what you have: guest booking, Outlook, and iOS Calendar.

1) Airline alerts as a guest (no account needed)
On a browser (phone or computer):
1. Go to Kenya Airways → “Manage Booking” or “Manage Trip.”
2. Enter:
   - Booking/confirmation: KQ8M2K4  
   - Last name: Brown  
3. Open the booking and look for “Contact details” / “Passenger details” / “Notifications.”
4. Make sure:
   - Email: keisha.brown@usace.army.mil  
   - Phone: 504-555-2931 (select SMS/text if there’s an option)  
Once that’s saved, Kenya Airways will send you:
   - Departure time changes  
   - Gate changes  
   - Delay/cancellation/diversion notices  

2) iOS Calendar alerts (on your iPhone)
1. Open Calendar → tap the “+” to create a new event.
2. Title: “KQ456 JFK → NBO (Kenya Airways).”
3. Start: set to your local JFK departure time on 2025-04-12.  
4. End: set to arrival time, or just a few hours later (for context).
5. Location: “JFK Terminal D Gate D8 (check for changes).”
6. Notes (optional but useful):
   - Conf: KQ8M2K4  
   - Flight: KQ456, JFK → NBO  
7. Tap “Alert”:
   - Set one alert for 3 hours before  
   - Add a second alert (tap Alert again) for 1 hour before  
8. Check that the event is on an iCloud/Exchange calendar that syncs to your phone.

3) Outlook email alerts so you notice any flight changes

If you mainly use Outlook desktop:
1. Find your flight confirmation email (from Kenya Airways or the booking site).
2. Right-click it → “Rules” → “Create Rule…”.
3. Under “When I get email with all of the selected conditions”:
   - Check “From [airline/agency]”  
   - Optionally check “Subject contains” and add: KQ456 or “Nairobi”  
4. Under “Do the following”:
   - Check “Display in the New Item Alert window”  
   - (Optional) “Play a selected sound”  
   - (Optional) “Assign it to the category” and create/use a “Travel/Flights” category  
5. Save the rule and apply to existing messages if prompted.

If you mainly use Outlook on the web:
1. Click the gear icon → “Mail” → “Rules” / “Email rules.”
2. Create a new rule:
   - Name: “Flight alerts KQ456”  
   - Condition: “From” contains the airline/agency; and/or “Subject includes” KQ456 or “flight status”  
   - Actions:  
     - Mark as “Important” or “Pin”  
     - Assign to a “Travel/Flights” category (optional)  
3. Save the rule.

With this setup:
- Airline: pushes time/gate/delay/cancel/divert changes to your email and phone.  
- iOS Calendar: reminds you well before departure.  
- Outlook: makes any flight-change email impossible to miss.
